chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali al-Naqid narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Aslami narrated to me from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said:
I heard Abu Dharr, and at that time Uthman had expelled him to al-Rabadhah, so the people said to him: O Abu Dharr! Rejoice, for this is little in the way of Allah, the Exalted.

He said: How insignificant this is (in the way of Allah)! But how will you be when al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) is killed – or he said slaughtered – in such a terrible way? By Allah, no killing will be greater than his killing in Islam after the killing of the Caliph.
And indeed Allah will unsheathe His sword against this nation and will never sheathe it again, and He will send an avenger [a standing one] from his progeny who will take revenge upon the people.

And if you knew what would befall the inhabitants of the seas, the dwellers of the mountains in the thickets and hills, and the people of the sky from his killing, you would cry by Allah until your souls expire.

And there is no sky through which the soul of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passes but seventy thousand angels are alarmed for him; they stand up in a standing in which their joints tremble until the Day of Judgment.
And there is no cloud that passes, thundering and lightninging, but it curses his killer.
And there is no day but his soul is presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and they meet one another.

key_terms.الرَّبَذَة: The place of exile for Abu Dharr near Mecca
key_terms.الْخَلِيفَة: The Caliph (referring to Uthman in this context)
key_terms.تَزْهَقَ أَنْفُسُكُمْ: Your souls expire / you die of grief
key_terms.نَاقِماً: An avenger / one who stands to take revenge

ai.seo_question: What are the cosmic signs and angelic reactions to the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Kamil al-Ziyarat highlights Abu Dharr al-Ghifari’s prophetic insight into the cosmic significance of Imam Husayn’s martyrdom, framing it as a pivotal event that permanently alters the spiritual and political trajectory of the Ummah. The text emphasizes the universal resonance of this sacrifice, where natural phenomena and celestial beings bear witness, reinforcing the Shia theological view of Husayn’s death as a transformative moment of divine justice and eternal remembrance.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. Abul Ḥusain Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Ali Al-Nāqid narrated to me from ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Aslami, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Urwah ibn Zubayr, who said:
On the day when ‘Uthmān expelled Abā Dhar to Rabadhah, people said to him, “O Abā Dhar! Rejoice, for verily this (suffering) is little in the way of Allāh, the Exalted.”

Abū Dhar replied: How insignificant this (suffering) is (in the way of Allāh)! But how will you feel when Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) is killed – or he said slaughtered – in such a terrible way?! I swear to Allāh that no killing will be greater than the killing of Ḥusain (a.s.) in (the history of) Islam.

Verily Allāh will unsheathe His sword against this nation and He will never sheathe it again. Verily Allāh will send an avenger from the progeny of Ḥusain (a.s.) who will seek revenge against the people.

I swear to Allāh that If you knew about (the grief) which will overcome the inhabitants of the seas, the mountains, the hills, the trees, and the heavens as a result of the killing of Ḥusain (a.s.), you would cry so (intensely) that your soul would leave (your bodies).

Seventy thousand angels will be alarmed in every sky through which the soul of Ḥusain (a.s.) will pass (after he will be killed). They will all stand up (for him) while their joints will be shaking (in awe of Ḥusain (a.s.)) until the Day of Judgment.
Every cloud that passes, each (roar of) thunder, and every (strike of) lightning curses the killers of Ḥusain (a.s.).
Every day the soul of Ḥusain (a.s.) is presented to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and they meet one another.
